column1: # The starting violation list of Broiler.RegEx's architecture tests: every violation that a rule SL1 to SL10 or a
# contract check C1, C3 or C5 of rules.register.json finds in the library on the day the tests were filed, 2026-10-25,
# at work package SJL-11.2 of the shared JavaScript libraries programme, at the code 0.1.0-preview.4 was packed from.
# Broiler.VM's JSD-0081 (section X3) lists the conventions these breach, and requirements R1 to R11 close them.
# Each rule's test asserts its rows in both directions: a violation the rule finds that is not here fails it, and so
# does a row the rule no longer finds. A change that removes a violation removes its row in the same change; no change
# adds one. SJL-11.2 shrinks the list to none, and bundle sjl-11-001's check E-3 holds it empty at the candidate reading.
# Where a rule reads where a violation is - SL1's assembly half, SL3, SL4 and C5 from the IL and the PDB's sequence
# points, SL5 from the NoWarn and WarningsNotAsErrors elements of the project file and of every build file of the
# repository its evaluation imports - its test asserts the row place by place as well: every place the rule finds is
# cited once, and every cited place is one the rule finds, so a row the rule still finds but at no place fails too. A
# call of a listed member in a statement of its own is a new place and fails the test, and so does a citation left on a
# line that no longer holds the violation, although the row's wording is the same in both. A place has two limits, which
# AssemblyFacts states: it is a statement, so a second use inside a statement that already holds one is not a new place;
# and it is where an instruction names the member, its declaring type or a type operand, so a use that names a type or
# an assembly only in a signature, a field or local type or a generic argument is no place at all. Review sees those
# uses. Every other row's violation names its one place: a static field, a public member or type, a file, a package, a
# Columns, tab-separated: the rule or check; the violation, exactly as the rule words it; a token the source holds where
# the violation is; and the places, path:line, space-separated, one line of each (a statement can span several).
# RuleRegisterTests checks that each cited line holds the token, so a citation moves with the code; the rule's own test
# decides whether the violation, and each place of it, is still there. A comment line here names a row's repair.

column1: # RegexMatch.Empty is every no-match result of the process, and its NamedGroups is a new Dictionary behind
# IReadOnlyDictionary, which a caller can cast and change for every later no-match. The repair: an empty read-only
# dictionary, ReadOnlyDictionary<string, RegexGroup>.Empty or FrozenDictionary<string, RegexGroup>.Empty, so that the
# initializer creates nothing mutable. The plan gives this row to no task. Its row 2.3 asks for no mutable static
# (convention 7), but 2.3's area is Parsing/, Ast/ and Unicode/, not Matching/; row 2.4c deletes Matching/, while row
# 2.9 and decision D12 keep the string-bearing RegexMatch, so the class outlives both. The owner is unassigned and is
# decided at task 2.3; row 2.9's check, an empty list, is the latest change in which the row can leave.
